Initially, Bushby planned to finish the journey much earlier, but visa and financial difficulties extended the adventure. Periodically, he veered off his route to earn money and then returned to his stopping point.

Main Points
⏺ A watch-only wallet lets users monitor balances and transactions without holding private keys
⏺ This setup is useful for large portfolios, cold storage, and address analysis
⏺ This post explains why monitoring assets doesn't require spending access

1️⃣ Core Idea — the app receives a public wallet address and displays its assets and transaction history.
2️⃣ Why It Helps — users can monitor long-term holdings without connecting the device that stores their private keys.
3️⃣ Use Cases — cold wallets, corporate treasuries, whale monitoring, and crypto portfolio accounting.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — the app cannot sign transactions without a key, but it may collect information about your addresses and financial activity.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — add only public addresses, verify supported networks, and never enter a seed phrase just to view balances.


Final Thoughts

You don't need to give an app control over your crypto just to monitor it. Separating viewing from signing reduces situations where private keys are exposed to unnecessary risk.

🌐 Blockstream CEO Adam Back has renewed his criticism of Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 110 (BIP-110), arguing that attempts to impose controversial network changes have repeatedly failed to gain market support. In a November 3 post on X, Back referenced earlier commentary from Bitcoin advocate Francis Pouliot while addressing supporters of the proposed Bitcoin fork.

📌 “Attempts to impose your views on bitcoin get market rejected,” Back wrote, pointing to previous disputes over Bitcoin’s rules. He described Pouliot’s commentary as a “masterclass on bitcoin reality” and said discussions about Bitcoin’s established rules were intended to help people understand immutability. Back’s latest comments followed renewed discussion about BIP-110, a proposal designed to restrict certain forms of non-financial data on Bitcoin.

➡️ He argued that the market would resist efforts to override consensus, even when supporters believed their proposed changes were beneficial.Back further claimed that BIP-110 “failed the first gate hard” because of what he described as serious technical problems. Hormuz Has a Guest List

Iran is offering selected countries passage through the waterway it has restricted. A senior Iranian lawmaker calls them exemptions, but Indian and Chinese ships must pay, while Qatari vessels cross free. For some guests, “exempt” apparently means eligible to receive an invoice.

The lawmaker named India, China, Iraq, and Qatar as beneficiaries. India, he said, helps supply medicines, and China provides political support. He did not say whether Iraqi ships pay.

The exemptions may be more pitch than policy. Argus reports that neither Iran’s government nor the Revolutionary Guards has formally confirmed them, and shipping data do not show unrestricted passage. Tehran’s permission also does nothing about the separate U.S. naval blockade.

Below the shipping lanes, another pressure point is drawing attention. The Financial Times reported that at least four Iran-linked vessels lingered near submarine cable routes in the Gulf of Oman after Tehran threatened digital infrastructure. No sabotage has been reported.

Iran is selling access to an international waterway as a favor. The business model only works if passage stays uncertain enough that permission has a price.

👀 Justin Sun becomes PEPE’s largest individual holder, Arkham says 

🌐 Tron founder Justin Sun has accumulated nearly 3% of PEPE’s supply, with blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence identifying approximately $51.25 million worth of the memecoin across his known and suspected wallets. According to an October 27 Arkham Intelligence report, the tokens entered Sun-linked wallets over the previous 10 days, making him the largest individual PEPE holder outside cryptocurrency exchanges.

🔗 The firm estimated his combined holdings at 2.82% of PEPE’s supply, although some wallets included in its calculations were attributed to Sun through blockchain analysis. At the time, PEPE had a market capitalization of approximately $1.81 billion, with exchanges controlling several of the largest known holdings.

📊 Binance held $337.5 million worth of PEPE, representing 18.7% of the supply, followed by Robinhood with $150.9 million, or 8.37%. Coinbase and OKX accounted for another 5.03% and 4.15%, respectively. Unlike Sun’s attributed holdings, exchange balances generally include assets held on behalf of customers, meaning their large positions do not necessarily represent investments made by the platforms themselves.
